current_episode.title: #49 Miami Is the Fastest-Growing Luxury City in America. She's Building the Infrastructure to Save It | Anya Freeman, Founder & CEO of Kind Designs

guest.bio_context: Anya Freeman is originally from Ukraine, moved to Israel, then to the United States after her father received a special talent visa to work with a space program. She attended law school at the University of Miami on a scholarship and worked as a litigator and prosecutor before launching Kind Designs. She left her legal career after witnessing accelerating flooding in her Miami community and decided the legal system alone could not fix the problem. Kind Designs has been named Startup of the Year by Fast Company and has won the Times Innovation Award of the Year.

pending_qa.q: What are the three key selling points of Kind Designs living seawalls for luxury real estate partners?
pending_qa.r: Anya Freeman identifies three selling points for luxury partners: sustainability, as many hotel groups and luxury developments have formal sustainability goals; aesthetics, because living seawalls are visually striking compared to the flat concrete slabs typically found even on multi-million dollar properties; and customization, as Kind Designs works with hotel groups and luxury buildings to create seawalls that match the brand or building's aesthetic identity, as demonstrated by their project with Pagani.

pending_qa.q: How much funding has Kind Designs raised and who are its investors?
pending_qa.r: Kind Designs has raised approximately $22 million in total funding, including a $10 million round closed just before the episode was recorded. The investor base is largely composed of Florida-based investors with personal experience of flooding and coastal real estate, along with former mayors, former congressmen, former commissioners, and lobbying groups, as well as construction professionals in coastal cities like Miami and New York City. High-profile investors include Mark Cuban.

pending_qa.q: What legislation has been passed to incentivize living seawalls in South Florida?
pending_qa.r: Miami-Dade County passed a law, championed by then-commissioner Eileen Higgins, exempting living seawall projects from mandatory environmental mitigation requirements such as riprap installation, making Kind Designs seawalls effectively cheaper than traditional alternatives. The City of Miami followed by offering 50% off building permit fees when a living seawall is shown in project plans. At the time of recording, the City of Fort Lauderdale was voting on a measure to offer 100% off building permit application fees for projects incorporating a living seawall.

pending_qa.q: How does Kind Designs use 3D printing technology to manufacture seawalls at scale?
pending_qa.r: Unlike large-scale 3D printing for houses, which uses on-site gantry-type robots, Kind Designs operates an indoor factory near the Miami River with four robots printing seawalls continuously in a factory-style production line. The company plans to expand to six robots within the next quarter. The entire product can be produced by the robots, and the freedom of design this enables allows for biomimicry textures and custom aesthetics that were previously unachievable with conventional manufacturing, with the full production line representing an investment of a few million dollars capable of generating three times that amount in annual revenue.

pending_qa.q: How did Anya Freeman's background as a litigator give her a competitive advantage as a startup founder?
pending_qa.r: Freeman credits her litigation background primarily for her storytelling ability, developed through competitive courtroom advocacy before judges and juries. She applied this skill to pitching investors, recruiting team members, and engaging customers, describing her fundraising presentations as more like a TED talk than a formulaic pitch. She also leveraged her legal knowledge to work with local legislators to pass codes and incentives that created favorable regulatory conditions for living seawalls, which she identifies as a key driver of Kind Designs' scalability.

pending_qa.q: Which luxury hospitality and real estate brands is Kind Designs currently working with?
pending_qa.r: Kind Designs is working on seawall projects for clients including the Ritz-Carlton, Mandarin Oriental, and the Fontainebleau. The company also completed a custom seawall project for Pagani, the luxury car brand building a residential building in Miami, where the seawall design was created to match the building's aesthetics. Additionally, Kind Designs has closed a major contract with the US Navy.

pending_qa.q: What is the gender diversity situation in the seawall construction industry and how has Anya Freeman navigated it?
pending_qa.r: Anya Freeman states she has yet to meet a single other woman working in the seawall construction space, noting that men have been building seawalls since 1904. She approached entry into the industry with respect, bringing established generational seawall contractors — many of them third- or fourth-generation family businesses — onto the team as investors and advisors. She attributes part of Kind Designs' design innovation, including the focus on aesthetics and ecological inclusivity, to applying a fresh, outside perspective to an industry that had not been challenged in over a century.

pending_qa.q: What is Anya Freeman's broader vision for Kind Designs and Miami's role in global coastal resilience?
pending_qa.r: Freeman states her ambition is to build the first female unicorn company in Miami and to make South Florida a global model for coastal construction innovation. She rejects the narrative that coastal cities like Miami are inevitably doomed by rising sea levels, arguing instead that the greatest challenges present the greatest opportunities. She frames Miami's choice as becoming either an example or a lesson for the rest of the world, with Kind Designs' technology serving as critical infrastructure for the city's luxury ecosystem and long-term viability.
